earned_by: The owner approved the main route: test whether the two-literal shielding identity (a lone odd loop along c has the same count in the twists q and q + PD(c)) survives for the winding contradictions of three-place tiling worlds, with exact counts on the smallest tori. Scratch scoping, all on the 3 x 3 torus unless stated. (1) The event 'the cylinder along c contradicts' fails the identity even in the two-literal orientation world (115832 vs 60456), because it includes crosses; the lone event (exactly one of the three cylinders contradicts) does not. (2) For placement 63, lone lines match the lone loops of the square-lattice orientation model in all classes and twists on 3 x 3, 3 x 4 and 4 x 3 (twist shifted by (L mod 2, M mod 2)); these runs of placement 63 on 3 x 4 and 4 x 3 are seen. (3) Every dual pair of the four orientation placements with nonzero counts is equal (2028 = 2028). (4) Equalities first seen at three places (placements 109, 123 and 95) are explained by vertex flips, which change literal signs and, on odd sides, the twist, composed with lattice symmetries. With these maps, all 22 unexplained nonzero dual pairs of three-place placements and all 4 of shared-coin placements are unequal (for example 6 vs 468, 24 vs 7308, 942 vs 876). Nothing else was computed on the fresh tori.
question: On triangular tori of sides 3 and 4, enumerated exhaustively, are the counts of lone line contradictions along a class c equal in the two twists q and q + PD(c) that are odd on c, and does the answer separate the two-literal orientation worlds (equal, by the shielding theorem) from three-place and shared-coin worlds (unequal unless a symmetry relates the twists)?

public_inputs.model: as in TRIPLE-TWIST-20261023-001B-E001: one fair visible bit x per triangle of the L x M triangular torus (no shear), hidden values on the vertices; a triangle allows the gauged patterns R when x = 0 and their complements when x = 1; up triangles ((i, j), (i+1, j), (i+1, j+1)) and down triangles ((i, j), (i, j+1), (i+1, j+1)) with corners (a, b, c) in that order; twist (alpha, beta) gauges each corner by alpha k1 + beta k2 mod 2 from its deck offsets (k1, k2), relative to the first corner
public_inputs.placements: the 54 TILING placements of artifacts/TRIPLE-TWIST-20261023-001B/TRIPLE-TWIST-20261023-001B-E001_contact_census/rows.jsonl, typed: orientation (63, 119, 187, 207: one clause of two literals on the square-lattice pair (a, b) or (b, c)), diagonal-clause (95, 175: one clause on (a, c)), shared-coin (the other 18 placements of kind pair: several clauses share one bit) and three (the 30 placements of kind three)
public_inputs.tori: 3 x 3 (family F_seen); 3 x 4, 4 x 3 and 4 x 4 (family F_fresh). All 54 placements on the first three; on 4 x 4 one placement per orbit of the maps below (19 orbits)
public_inputs.classes: (1, 0), (0, 1) and (1, 1) in deck coordinates (periods (L, 0), (0, M) and (L, M))
public_inputs.programs: tshield.c (cylinder transfers) and labels.c (orientation model of TWIST-MAP-20261023-001B-E001, for the control), compiled by run.py

definitions: The cylinder along c is the infinite cover of the torus whose deck group is generated by c's period. A world contradicts on the torus or a cylinder when no hidden assignment exists; on the cylinder this holds iff some finite part contradicts. Both are computed by a transfer over the levels of phi(i, j) = c2 M i - c1 L j, which vanishes on c: the torus has an assignment iff the period relation has a fixed point, the cylinder iff it has a cycle. lone_c: the cylinder along c contradicts and the other two do not. cross: the torus contradicts and no cylinder does (this includes lines along classes other than the three). A twist fits when a doubly allowed assignment exists (every triangle's gauged pattern allowed for both values of x). The dual pair of c: the twists odd on c relative to every fitting twist; when there are exactly two they differ by PD(c) = (c2, c1) mod 2. Maps: a lattice symmetry of the torus (12 on 3 x 3 and 4 x 4, 2 on 3 x 4 and 4 x 3) followed by a vertex flip (flip the hidden value of every vertex of the fundamental domain with alpha i + beta j odd; on odd sides this adds (alpha L, beta M) mod 2 to the twist), whenever up and down triangles end with the same relations up to complement. These maps form a group and preserve every count. A dual pair is explained when such a map takes (R, q1, c) to (R, q2, +-c).

predictions.P1_theorem: theorem-predicted (ticket B, the cylinder form of TRIPLE-TWIST-20261023-001A Theorem 5): no world contradicts in a fitting twist, and the cylinder along c contradicts only in twists odd on c relative to every fitting twist
predictions.P2_orientation_shield: theorem-predicted (LOOP-SHIELD-20261023-001C Theorem 1, with the identification of lone lines and line events argued in ticket B and checked by the control on placement 63): every dual pair of every orientation placement has equal lone counts
predictions.P3_three_place: scoping-predicted: on the fresh tori, no unexplained dual pair of a three-place placement with a nonzero count has equal lone counts
predictions.P4_shared_coin: scoping-predicted: on the fresh tori, no unexplained dual pair of a shared-coin placement with a nonzero count has equal lone counts
predictions.reported: per placement, torus and twist: the counts of torus contradictions, cylinder contradictions and lone lines per class, and crosses; the fitting twists; per dual pair the lone and cylinder counts and whether a map explains it; a tally per family and type

controls: (i) every row covers all 2^(2LM) configurations; (ii) whenever the row transfer finds no fixed point, neither do the column and diagonal transfers (the torus test agrees across three sweep directions); (iii) on each torus, in each class and twist, the lone count of placement 63 equals the lone-loop count of the square-lattice orientation model computed by labels.c, a different program on a different model (clusters of the twisted double cover of an orientation), in the twist shifted by (L mod 2, M mod 2)
decision_rule: If a control fails, the result is invalid. Refuted if P1 or P2 fails. Supported if P1, P2, P3 and P4 hold. Partially supported if P1 and P2 hold and P3 or P4 fails; the exceptions are listed pair by pair.
stop_rule: Enumerate the four tori in order, writing rows as each torus finishes; then check the controls and decide. No adaptive extension: a larger torus would need sampling and is out of scope.
environment: CPython 3 standard library and gcc (C99) for the two C programs
red_team_r0: Counts are exact: every configuration is enumerated, so equality and inequality are exact on these tori; the tori are tiny and a pattern here need not persist on larger ones.

lone_c tracks three classes; contradictions along other classes, such as (1, -1) or (1, 2), count as crosses, so lone_c is a restricted analog of the two-literal line event; the control checks the identification for placement 63.
The maps used to explain pairs might not be all the count-preserving maps; an unexplained equality is a candidate for a new identity, not proof of one.
P1 and P2 are theorem-predicted; a failure would point to a code error or a gap in the theorem or in the identification.
The transfer window is at most 16 states (4 bits); the program exits rather than truncate a larger window.
4 x 4 covers orbit representatives only; their orbits are computed with the same maps that explain pairs, and the checker verifies the maps explicitly, triangle by triangle.
The scoping data (3 x 3, and placement 63 on 3 x 4 and 4 x 3) are seen; P3 and P4 are judged on the fresh tori only.
nonclaims: Exact counts on four small tori; no asymptotic statement.
No claim that three-place worlds have no wall at all; only the dual-pair identity for lone lines along three classes is tested.
Lattices and twists are declared; nothing is said about space or physics.
forbidden_inputs: Expected counts, equalities or verdicts as inputs to the run
